headline: NYC plans record 160 car-free Trick-or-Streets locations for October
dek: The citywide Halloween program will bring free activities, school events and neighborhood walking tours to Open Streets and plazas across all five boroughs.
body: New York City is expanding its Trick-or-Streets program to a record 160 car-free Open Streets and plazas this October, giving families in all five boroughs a month of Halloween and fall events instead of a single-night celebration.

The city says the locations will host trick-or-treating, face painting, live entertainment and games. The New York City Department of Transportation also plans to distribute about 75,000 pieces of candy. ABC7 New York reported the same announcement Wednesday, Sept. 30, and described the program as the city's largest Trick-or-Streets event to date: https://abc7ny.com/post/mayor-mamdani-announces-nycs-largest-trick-streets-new-york/19892758/

The effort is designed around temporary changes to public space. Community organizations, schools and cultural groups will turn selected streets and plazas into pedestrian-oriented gathering places, while the Municipal Art Society of New York will offer free guided walking tours focused on neighborhood history, architecture and public spaces. Street Lab is also partnering with NYC DOT and city schools on Halloween-themed play and creative activities at selected school sites.

Five signature events anchor the schedule. Brooklyn's Hillel Plaza celebration is set for Oct. 22 from 2 to 6 p.m.; Staten Island's Water Street Open Street follows Oct. 24 from noon to 5 p.m.; and Queens' Austin Street Open Street is scheduled for Oct. 25 from 2 to 7 p.m. Manhattan's Canal Street Open Street and Division Plaza event is planned for Oct. 28 from 3 to 7 p.m., while the Bronx's James Baldwin Plaza event is scheduled for Halloween, Oct. 31, from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m.

The Department of Transportation's event page lists additional neighborhood programs beginning Oct. 3, including activities on Vanderbilt Avenue in Brooklyn and Castleton Avenue on Staten Island. The calendar includes block parties, parades, dog events and school-linked programming throughout the month. NYC DOT says individual events can be delayed or canceled because of weather, so families should check the official calendar before traveling: https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/pedestrians/trickorstreets.shtml

The month-long format matters because the program is also a test of how New York uses streets beyond their usual transportation role. The city's announcement says the participating groups will use the spaces for community celebrations and, in some cases, to support local foot traffic and neighborhood businesses. The setup gives organizers control over their own programming while the city coordinates the street closures and works with partner agencies.

Mayor Zohran Kwame Mamdani and NYC DOT Commissioner Mike Flynn announced the expansion on Sept. 30. This is the fifth year of Trick-or-Streets, according to NYC DOT, which says the initiative is meant to add pedestrian space during one of the busiest periods for New York streets. The full map and schedule remain the best guide to what is happening on a particular block, because the 160 locations will not all be active at the same time. The primary announcement is available from the NYC Mayor's Office: https://www.nyc.gov/mayors-office/news/2026/09/mayor-mamdani-announces-largest-ever-trick-or-streets-with-160-c
author: NorthEast News Desk
seoDescription: New York City's record 160-location Trick-or-Streets program will bring Halloween events, school activities and walking tours to all five boroughs in October.
